title: 2026-07-18 CUDA launch timeouts and quantized KV-cache fallback - Helmholtz Systems
summary: Deep-dive on intermittent CUDA LAUNCH_TIMEOUT errors observed on quantized model variants, interactions with KV cache prefetch and batching, and recommended graceful degradation + retry semantics for Helmholtz's private deployment. Agreed to run kernel-level trace and add a reproducible harness. Next steps include shared logs, trial config for dedicated capacity, and follow-up bench with debug builds.
topics: Quantized model variants (int8/4bit) causing different memory/launch behavior
KV cache prefetch timings and eviction interplay with batching
Retry semantics, exponential backoff, and canary fallback to fp16 model
Observability: watchdogs, GPU driver logs, perf counters
VPC / on-prem constraints: kernel driver versions and restricted syscalls
next_steps: Helmholtz to upload /var/log/nvidia-driver and dmesg excerpts to shared folder (link: https://redwood.link/helm-logs)
Redwood SE to provide a reproducible micro-benchmark harness and a debug build with extra kernel traces by 2026-07-22
Schedule bench run on Helmholtz dedicated pool for 2 hours (Jordan to coordinate schedule)
Agree on temporary fallback policy: 10s launch timeout -> try 1) smaller batch 2) switch to fp16 model 3) throttle prefetch

meeting_header: Date: 2026-07-18 15:30 UTC | Duration: 62 mins | Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - Helmholtz), Sofia Alvarez (Platform Eng), Daniel Park (ML Eng), Ava Winters (SRE)
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. We'll dive straight into the launch-timeout pattern you hit. Priya and I joined to walk through kernel traces and retry logic.

00:28 Marcus Lee: Yeah thanks. We've been seeing intermittent CUDA_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT on our on-prem cluster, mostly when running the int8 quantized variant at scale. It looks like prefetch + big batches triggers it but it's not consistent.
00:46 Priya Raman: ok, can you describe the environment — driver/kernel versions, GPU type, and whether the nodes are multi-tenanted? Those things matter for the watchdog behavior.

01:10 Sofia Alvarez: We're on Ubuntu 22.04 with 525.x driver, A100s in a private rack, nodes are single-tenant for this workload but we do run other infra processes. Kube version is 1.25, CRI is containerd.

01:34 Daniel Park: And the workload — it's a chat-like long context workload, lots of KV cache hits, we prefetch next blocks aggressively to keep latency down. When we ramp qps to peak, launch timeouts spike.

02:00 Priya Raman: Prefetching plus heavy KV eviction can shadow memory and cause transient kernel scheduling pressure. In some drivers, a long-running kernel or an overload of concurrent launches will trip the watchdog. Do you have dmesg / driver logs when the timeouts happen?

02:22 Marcus Lee: We have some dmesg snippets, I'll upload after. The error sometimes shows as "CUDA error 719" in our app logs — I think that's LAUNCH_TIMEOUT. The weird bit is only int8 shows it, fp16 is mostly fine.

02:45 Jordan Ellis: That's interesting — quantized kernels often change kernel launch patterns and memory footprint. int8 kernels can be more compute intense per launch or use different kernels that might be less preemptible.
03:05 Sofia Alvarez: We also saw GPU context resets occasionally but not consistently. Not a full node reboot, just process-level failures and retries handled by our runner.

03:25 Priya Raman: A few hypotheses: 1) kernel busy/long-running causing watchdog to think driver is hung, 2) memory overcommit from aggressive prefetch leading to OOM-like behavior that stresses the driver, 3) a specific kernel in the quantized path hitting a pathologically slow branch. We'll need kernel traces and nvprof/perf counters.
03:56 Daniel Park: We can run nvprof but it's heavy. Is there a lighter repro, or flags to enable runtime trace to capture launch latency only?

04:10 Priya Raman: We'll provide a debug runtime with optional trace points and a micro-benchmark harness — it will emit per-launch timestamps, queue depths, and prefetch/eviction events. That should isolate whether it's launch latency distribution or memory pressure.
04:36 Marcus Lee: Another datapoint — when we reduce batch size by half, the problem frequency drops dramatically. But latency per-request goes up and cost increases, so it's a tradeoff.

04:52 Jordan Ellis: Right. That's the usual latency-vs-cost tradeoff. For production, we can propose graceful degradation: on N consecutive launch timeouts or a launch latency P95 crossing threshold, fallback to fp16 variant for that route, or temporarily reduce prefetch concurrency.
05:14 Sofia Alvarez: Would fallback add jitter? We have strict SLOs around median latency, so we need deterministic behavior.
05:27 Priya Raman: We can make the policy deterministic: detect condition, mark session-level switch for next X requests, and ensure canary rollbacks. Also add a short cool-down to prevent flip-flop.
05:43 Daniel Park: Sounds OK. What about retry semantics? Currently we retry 2x with fixed 2s backoff, which sometimes masks the problem but then floods during recovery.

06:00 Priya Raman: Exponential backoff with jitter is safer. Also add an early abort if we detect driver-level LAUNCH_TIMEOUT patterns — don't retry indefinitely. Redwood runtime has a configurable policy: initial_delay, max_retries, abort_on_driver_error boolean.
06:21 Marcus Lee: Can we push that into our runtime? We're on a private deployment so patching the runtime is on us; Redwood recommended a config we can flip.

06:33 Jordan Ellis: We'll send the recommended config snippet. Also watch for kernel preemption support and driver upgrades; some driver versions have better watchdog behavior. We'll add driver version suggestions in the doc.
06:50 Sofia Alvarez: On the topic of KV cache — we do aggressive prefetching of upcoming prompts. Prefetch spawns extra kernels and moves pages, could that push the driver into too many launches?

07:06 Priya Raman: Yes, prefetch increases concurrent kernel activity and can increase launch rate. If the GPU is already saturated, launches queue and sometimes the watchdog thinks the driver is unresponsive. Two mitigations: a) throttle prefetch concurrency based on queue depth and b) prefer smaller more frequent prefetches rather than large bulk prefetch.
07:34 Daniel Park: Our prefetch logic is heuristics-based. Could Redwood's runtime provide adaptive throttling? We'd rather not hard-code static limits.

07:45 Priya Raman: We have workload-aware throttling proposals — runtime monitors in-flight launches and reduces prefetch window when launch latency P95 climbs. We can share a config and a patch for Helmholtz to test.
08:00 Marcus Lee: Great. Another question: when the timeout occurs, our process exits and k8s restarts container. Is there a graceful rescue mode to avoid full restart?

08:12 Priya Raman: Two options: catch the launch error at the inference worker, and try a local fallback (reduce batch or model) without crashing container, or implement process-level watchdog that collects logs and restarts in a controlled manner. The first is preferable.
08:30 Jordan Ellis: For private deployments we usually recommend the in-process fallback plus a small circuit-breaker to avoid repeated failures.
09:00 Sofia Alvarez: About observability — what exact counters/logs should we capture? We want a minimal set to send you.

09:12 Priya Raman: Per-launch timestamps (enqueue, launch, completion), GPU memory high-water mark, kernel runtime histogram, driver dmesg with timestamps, and nvml GPU utilization + ECC errors. Also any core dumps.
09:28 Daniel Park: We'll collect those. We'll probably need a short debug window if it affects prod.

09:40 Marcus Lee: One more weirdness — sometimes we see the error correlated with an unrelated tenant job that spikes IO on the node. Even though nodes are single-tenant for inference, infra tasks run on the same physical server.

09:55 Priya Raman: IO spikes can cause kernel scheduling stalls especially if pageable memory is involved. If prefetching pulls pages and the host IO is saturated, the driver might wait on PCIe transfers and appear hung.
10:08 Sofia Alvarez: We can try isolating the NIC/IO tasks from inference nodes. That might be a quick mitigation.

10:20 Jordan Ellis: Regarding quant kernels — sometimes int8 kernels use different fused ops and different shared memory patterns. If one kernel branch has a pathological loop, it can hold the SMs longer. Profiling will show that.

10:38 Priya Raman: We'll include kernel-level counters in the debug build to detect long-running warps or occupancy anomalies. Also check for mixed-precision intrinsics that might trigger non-preemptible ops.
10:56 Daniel Park: Is there a recommended fallback ordering? For example: 1) try smaller batch 2) throttle prefetch 3) switch to fp16 4) route to another region?

11:12 Priya Raman: Yes roughly that. Prefer local soft fixes first (batch/prefetch), then model variant fallback (fp16), then routing to a different pool or region. The routing step depends on capacity and cost.
11:32 Marcus Lee: For private on-prem, routing to another region isn't an option. We'd prefer deterministic local strategies.
11:45 Priya Raman: Understood. We'll prepare a deterministic policy you can embed: fixed-order fallback with cool-down windows and a telemetry flag so the console can surface which fallback was used.
12:00 Sofia Alvarez: About driver upgrades — can you give guidance which driver versions are more stable for our stack? We are stuck on 525 due to other dependencies.

12:12 Jordan Ellis: We'll note recommended driver matrix. Sometimes 525 has quirks; 535+ had improvements around preemption. But you need to validate with your infra dependencies. We'll provide a compatibility table.
12:30 Daniel Park: Can we talk about retry counts? Right now our client retries cause spikes because multiple requests re-queue at the same time.

12:44 Priya Raman: Add jitter and cap concurrent retries per node. e.g., token-bucket that allows X retries per minute. Also exponential backoff starting 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms works well with launch-timeout scenarios.
13:05 Marcus Lee: That makes sense. We'll update our client. Anything else on quantization interactions?

13:12 Priya Raman: Quantization sometimes increases cache coherence churn because KV cache fetches differ slightly in access patterns. Also smaller model weights change memory layout; combine that with prefetch and you get contention. We'll compare memory maps between fp16 and int8 runs.
13:35 Daniel Park: We can diff the memory maps — we'll add that to the logs we upload.
13:45 Sofia Alvarez: About the repro harness — can we run it in a controlled window and reproduce within 30 minutes? We want limited impact on prod.
13:56 Priya Raman: The harness aims to reproduce high qps with your workload shape. If it's tuned, we should see failure modes within an hour. We'll provide a low-impact mode first.
14:10 Jordan Ellis: Ok let's talk timeline: logs by EOD 7/20, Redwood SE debug build by 7/22, dedicated bench run week of 7/25. Is that acceptable?
14:22 Marcus Lee: Yes that works for us.

14:30 Priya Raman: One operational note — enable more granular watchdog metrics in your node exporter so we can see if the OS thinks processes are blocked. Also capture the container runtime logs around the timeouts.
14:45 Ava Winters: We'll get kubelet logs and containerd logs. We also have workload-level traces from OpenTelemetry that might help.

15:00 Jordan Ellis: Great. I'll send a meeting recap and the config snippets: recommended retry policy, prefetch throttle config, and fallback policy. Also a short checklist for driver/firmware data to collect.
15:14 Marcus Lee: Thanks. Quick question — is there any risk that switching to fp16 harms quality for our prompt sets in a measurable way?

15:27 Priya Raman: It can for some tasks; we'll run A/B evals on your prompt set during the bench. If degradation is unacceptable, we prefer throttling prefetch and smaller batches instead of model fallback.
15:45 Daniel Park: ok noted, we'll prioritize the evals.
16:00 Jordan Ellis: Any blockers from Helmholtz side to run the debug bench?
16:08 Ava Winters: We need written steps and a time window — we'll coordinate maintenance window with infra team.
16:18 Jordan Ellis: I'll send scheduling options.
16:25 Marcus Lee: One last thing — can Redwood's console surface when a fallback was used in the last 24 hours? That helps our triage.
16:36 Priya Raman: Yes we can add a short term telemetry tag: fallback_reason and fallback_model, that'll be visible in the console and logs.
16:50 Jordan Ellis: Perfect. We'll capture the action items and follow up. Thanks everyone.
17:00 Marcus Lee: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
17:10 Sofia Alvarez: Bye.
62:00 [meeting end] Automated note: recording stopped
